transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brought me in is that I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. I'm a software developer, and lately... I'll be trying to fix a rendering bug, and then a Slack ping, or maybe a color pattern on the screen, or even a siren outside just completely pulls me into a whole new idea. It happens before I can even finish typing a single line of code.
Would you say you've always been this easily distracted since childhood, or is this a new change from how you used to function?

I'm... I'm not really sure about when I was a kid, to be honest. I don't really remember it being an issue back then. But it's definitely a change from how I usually function now. I mean, I used to be able to just put my headphones on and code for hours without breaking focus. But lately, I just... I can't do that at all.
Along with this distractibility, have you noticed any changes in your mood, energy level, or need for sleep recently—like feeling unusually elated, energetic, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, actually. My mood has been... well, most days lately I just feel completely lit up. Like I have all this energy and I'm just unstoppable. It feels like Glendale has finally caught up with what I've been building, you know? 

But... I guess I've also been getting pretty irritable. If my wife or my coworkers try to slow me down with what they call "process," I just... I snap at them. I snap hard. I just don't have the patience for anyone holding me back right now.
Have you ever had a period in the past—lasting days or weeks—where you felt unusually high-energy and elated like this, or conversely, deeply depressed and low, before this current episode?

I haven't really noticed anything like that before. I mean, I don't think I've ever felt this energized in the past, and I don't really remember ever feeling deeply depressed or low for days or weeks either. This all feels pretty new to me.
How long has this period of feeling unusually energetic, elated, and irritable been going on so far—days, or weeks?
It's been going on for a while now. I'd say... about three months. It started right around the time my platform got selected for the Glendale showcase.

Have you found yourself believing things that others don't seem to believe—like having special powers, a special mission, or that people are watching or communicating with you in unusual ways—or have you seen or heard things that others around you don't seem to notice?

Well, I don't know about special powers or anything like that. But... I do know that some major museums and a couple of big investors are quietly circling my platform. I mean, it's obvious to me, even if other people don't see it yet. 

The language they used in the showcase announcements, the way they've been posting on Instagram... it all points directly to my work. And even some of the emails I've been getting at my day job, there are these subtle hints. It just lines up too perfectly to be a coincidence. They're definitely watching what I'm doing and getting ready to make a move.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a first-ever episode (no prior manic or depressive episodes) of elevated, expansive mood with increased energy, decreased need to slow down, irritability, and marked distractibility lasting approximately 3 months. This exceeds the 1-week threshold for mania and has caused clear functional impairment (conflict with spouse/coworkers, inability to sustain work focus). Additionally, the patient endorses grandiose and referential beliefs (museums/investors 'circling' his work, subtle hints in emails/social media confirming this) that are mood-congruent, non-bizarre but fixed and not shared by others, consistent with psychotic features occurring within the manic episode. Because this is a single, first lifetime mood episode rather than a recurrent pattern, this is coded as a manic episode with psychotic symptoms (F30.2) rather than bipolar disorder (F31.2), and the presence of psychotic features distinguishes it from F30.1.
